resumen: ## Ancient Egypt
The Ancient Egyptian civilisation developed **over 5000 years ago** (c3200 BCE–30 BCE). It is famous for huge buildings called **pyramids**.
## Egypt and the River Nile
- Egypt is in **North Africa**. The **Red Sea** is to the east and the **Mediterranean Sea** is to the north.
- Most of Egypt is **desert** with little or no rain.
- The **River Nile** flows **north** for **7000 km** through the whole of Egypt.
- Each year the Nile **flooded**. It left a thick layer of **mud** that made the land **fertile**, so people could grow plenty of food.
## The pharaohs
- **Pharaohs** were the kings or queens of Ancient Egypt. The pharaoh **owned all the land**, **made the laws** and received **taxes**.
- Over **170 pharaohs** ruled Egypt in **30 dynasties** (families of rulers).

- We remember pharaohs because people **wrote down** what they did and made **pictures** carved into rock or painted onto walls; some built **huge structures**, some were **warriors**, some were **women**.
## Timeline
- **3100 BCE** King **Narmer** united the two kingdoms of Egypt.
- **2650 BCE** first **step pyramid** built by **Djoser**.
- **2580–2560 BCE** **Great Pyramid** built at **Giza**.
- **1630–1523 BCE** the **Hyksos** people invaded.
- **1332 BCE** **Tutankhamun** came to power.
- **332 BCE** **Alexander the Great** invaded.
- **30 BCE** **Cleopatra**, the last Greek pharaoh, died.

resumen: ## Farming and the Nile
- **Fertile soil** near the Nile helped farmers grow crops.
- Farmers dug **channels** from the river to the fields and used a **shaduf** to lift water onto the fields.
## Crops
- **Cereals**: wheat and barley. **Vegetables**: onions, beans, cucumbers. **Fruit**: melons, pomegranates, grapes.
- Farmers gave part of their produce, especially **grain**, to the **government** as **tax**.
## Animals
- Working animals: **oxen** and **donkeys**. **Cows and goats** gave milk. **Ducks and geese** gave meat and eggs.
## Trade
- Egypt traded **grain, gold, papyrus, pottery and dates**.
- It **imported** metals, wood, gem stones, **incense**, **myrrh** and oils.
- Merchants used **boats** on the Nile, across the **Red Sea** and around the **Mediterranean Sea**, and carried some goods over land.
- Early merchant boats were made of **reeds**; later boats were made of **wood**.

resumen: ## A hierarchy
Ancient Egyptian **society** was organised as a **hierarchy**. A person's **job** marked their place in society.
- **Pharaoh** (top): had **complete power**.
- **Government officials, noblemen and religious leaders**: officials helped organise the country; nobles and religious leaders got **gifts and land** from the pharaoh.
- **Soldiers**: had respect; given **land when they retired**.
- **Scribes**: from **wealthy families**; wrote **official documents**.
- **Merchants**: supplied materials to craftspeople and **sold the finished goods**.
- **Craftspeople**: stonemasons, builders, carpenters, potters, jewellers, weavers.
- **Farmers, servants and slaves** (bottom): most people were **peasant farmers** on other people's land; servants were **paid**; slaves were **captured prisoners** or people from very poor families.
## Clothes
Light **linen** clothes (made from the **flax** plant) kept people **cool** and protected them from the sun.
## Houses
- Towns were built on **higher ground** to be safe from **flooding**.
- Houses were made of **bricks of mud and straw**, with **small, high windows** and a **reed roof** for shade.
- People used the **flat roof** for eating and sleeping. Inside was a family room with little furniture.
- Food was mainly **bread, fruit and vegetables**. **Goats** (milk) and **geese** (eggs) lived in the yard. People **hardly ever ate meat**.

resumen: ## The next life
- The Egyptians believed that after death people went to live **another life** in another place.
- Rich people's bodies were **preserved** by **mummification**. The preserved body is a **mummy**.
- The mummy was placed in a decorated coffin called a **sarcophagus**.
## The pyramids
- A pyramid was a special **tomb** to protect the body and the **treasures**. It was a symbol of **power and wealth**.
- Inside: a **burial chamber** and **passageways** designed to confuse **tomb robbers**.
- Boats carried the huge blocks up the **Nile**, so most pyramids were built **near the river**.
- Angled sides represent the **rays of the sun**.
- No-one is completely sure how they were built. Builders had to make a **level base**, organise workers to move **millions of stone blocks** and build the sides at the **correct angle**.
- The **Great Pyramid of Khufu** used more than **2 million** blocks and was covered in white **limestone**.
## The Valley of the Kings
- Pyramids were used until about **1540 BCE**. Later pharaohs were buried in the **Valley of the Kings**, on the **west bank of the Nile** opposite **Thebes**.
- **Tomb robbers** stole everything from most tombs.
## Tutankhamun
- Ruled **1332–1323 BCE**; not very important, but the most famous pharaoh today.
- His tomb was undisturbed for over **3000 years**. In **1922** the **Egyptologist Howard Carter** found it, full of **hundreds of objects**.

temas.titulo: 1.5 The Egyptian influence – evidence and inspiration
resumen: ## Hieroglyphics
- The Egyptians wrote with **hieroglyphics**: **pictures** that stand for words, sounds, objects, actions and ideas.
- Later they made forms of writing that were **easier and faster**. Alphabets used today **developed from** hieroglyphics.
## The Rosetta Stone
- Found in **1799** near the port of **Rosetta** (now **Rashid**).
- It had the **same text in three languages**; one was **Ancient Greek**, which scholars could read.
- After **20 years** of study, the Frenchman **Jean-François Champollion** made the first translation of hieroglyphics.
## Paintings and carvings
Wall paintings and carvings are **evidence** about the pharaohs and everyday life: **food, clothing, work and recreation**.
## Art as inspiration
- **Merchants and travellers** took Egyptian ideas to other countries: **Ancient Greece** and **17th- and 18th-century Europe**.
- The discovery of **Tutankhamun's tomb (1922)** created huge interest. Example: a **factory in London** built **1926–1928**.
## Mathematics
- Measurements based on **body parts** (e.g. the width of the **palm**).
- By about **2700 BCE** a **number system based on 10**. They knew **prime numbers, unit fractions and geometry**.
- A **calendar** of **12 months of 30 days** plus **5 extra feast days**.
